title: Enable content-addressable release blobs and Helm immutable upgrader for private-installer
author: Rafael Gutierrez
description: Motivation: make private-installer release delivery reproducible, auditable, and fast to rollback by switching pointers rather than rewriting channel manifests. This PR introduces a content-addressable (CA) blob index for release artifacts, KMS-backed signing of blob indexes, and an "immutable upgrader" Helm sidecar/Job that upgrades clusters by installing releases referenced by CA blob digests rather than mutable URLs. The CA index is an append-only manifest of artifacts with stable digests, upload timestamps, and cosign signatures. The upgrade flow moves from channel-based mutable manifests to digest-pinned artifacts while preserving compatibility with existing on-prem workflows via a migration shim. Changes include: 1) a new CA indexer micro-binary that enumerates built release blobs, computes digests, and emits a signed index; 2) Helm packaging adjustments so chart tarballs are uploaded with digest-based object names and the upgrader resolves artifacts by digest; 3) Terraform module additions that introduce a 'release_pointer' resource (a single transactional S3 object/key) and a 'rollback_trigger' boolean that forces the installer to switch pointers atomically for emergency rollbacks; 4) CI pipeline updates to sign indexes with KMS/cosign and publish delta shards for faster client pulls; 5) e2e tests that exercise upgrade and rollback using a local minio test fixture. Backwards compatibility: a migration controller reads the existing channel manifests and generates an initial CA index mapping; customers may opt-in to the CA mode. Security: all indexes are signed with customer KMS keys (private deployments) or with the org key for hosted CI; cosign verification is performed as part of the upgrader pre-flight. Rollback model: to roll back, the ops flow flips the release_pointer to the previous digest and notifies the upgrader; the upgrader will perform a reconcile based on the pointer change. Migration steps and rollback playbook are included in docs. Testing: unit coverage for indexer and Terraform module, integration job in CI that runs a full upgrade+rollback scenario, and staged canary validation. See linked Linear tickets for rollout staging and rollout gating. Breaking change: false. Merge rationale: reduces blast radius for upgrades and enables atomic rollbacks across environments.
commits: init: ca indexer prototype; feat(helm): digest-pinned chart packaging and upgrader job; feat(terraform): release_pointer resource and rollback_trigger; ci: sign-and-publish pipeline and delta shards; test: e2e upgrade/rollback harness and minio fixture; docs: migration and runbook
review_thread: Asha Mehta (reviewer): Can you clarify how the release_pointer interacts with existing autoscaling of buckets? Are there potential races on pointer writes?

Author (Rafael): Added a conditional lease acquisition in the Terraform module and documented the atomic pointer write semantics. Also updated the indexer to emit an upload token for multipart upload completion.
Jonas Rivera (reviewer): The cosign verification should be optional for air-gapped installs where KMS is unavailable. Add a toggle in values.yaml.
Author (Rafael): Added 'upgrader.verifySignatures' toggle and defaulted verification to on; documented operational tradeoffs in migration-runbook.md.
Priya Kapoor (reviewer): Integration test failed intermittently in CI due to minio time skew, recommend stable test fixture and retry logic.
Author (Rafael): Added time-sync step in the fixture and exponential backoff to the test harness; re-ran CI and greened tests.
ci_checks: integration-tests: flaky first run (minio time skew), re-run passed
release_notes: Introduces content-addressable release blobs, KMS/cosign-signed indexes, a Helm immutable upgrader that installs digest-pinned artifacts, and Terraform support for atomic release pointers and rollback triggers. Includes migration runbook and e2e rollback tests.
